messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — seeing a spike in fncall / tool-schema rejects over the last 10m. Reject rate up ~6x. Most of these are routed to the cheap-eu pool. Logs show `structured_validation: fail` + fallback to plain text.
maria: ugh. Any indication this is traffic skew or a model-version mismatch? :thinking:
lee: quick peek — the cheap-eu pool is running model v2.1 which has stricter schema enforcement enabled by default. Hosted default is v2.0 with permissive soft-validate. When routing policy changed last night, % routed to cheap-eu jumped from 8% -> 40%.
dana: are rejects actually causing customer-visible errors or just our internal fallbacks? alex: mostly internal fallbacks right now — we rewrite to unstructured and surface a warning. But a subset are hitting quota rejections in downstream tool adapters (they get unexpected shape => 422) which bubbles up as user errors.
sanjay: sample log:
```
ERROR tool_adapter: validation failed for call_id=abc123 model=v2.1 schema=payment_intent
payload: {"amount": "100"}
expected: {"amount": number}
fallback: unstructured_call
```
pm-oliver: this feels like an ops/regression from the routing tweak. Should we rollback routing or relax validation temporarily?
maria: two levers: routing + validation strictness. Routing rollback would reduce rejects quickly but hides the root mismatch. Relaxing strictness in v2.1 could be risky.
jess: console dashboards currently don't have a dedicated metric for `fncall_schema_reject_rate` by model+region. We only surface overall `invoke_errors`. That's why ops missed the pattern.
lee: quick proposal:
- add telemetry tag: `fncall.validation=reject|soft|pass` and emit per-request
- add metric `redwood.fncall.schema_reject_rate{model,region}` to Prometheus and Datadog
- increase sampling of full payload traces for rejects from 1% -> 10% for 1h after an incident
- expose a console toggle to temporarily set `strict_tool_schema` to false per deployment for canary rollbacks

alex: also add an alert: if reject_rate exceeds 1% in a region for 5m, page platform-oncall (pagerduty) and open an ops incident channel.
infra-bot: deploy bot: Notice: canary routing change deployed by @lee at 2026-03-20T19:40:12Z — routing.policy: cheap-eu weight 0.4
sanjay: fine. Immediate steps: (1) lee revert routing to previous weights (2) jess add the metric + dashboard panel for `fncall_schema_reject_rate` (3) dana and alex add reject-tag and increase trace sampling on those events
maria: for UX: console should show 5 latest raw payloads (redacted) for schema rejects with quick 'open in debugger' link. Also a button to 'temporarily relax validation for this model' with required audit log.
jess: will add dashboard panel and console mock. I'll put a low-fidelity wire by EOD.
dana: implementation note: keep sampling toggle in runtime config + make it local to the routing shard to avoid global cost surge. Use `runtime.config.toggles.fncall_trace_sampling`.
lee: reverted routing weights at 1718329200 — cheap-eu back to 8%.
pm-oliver: appreciate the quick rollback. Next: let's discuss longer-term: canary UX for validation strictness. We need a rollout flow: start soft-validate at 0% strictness -> canary 5% strict -> increase to 50% -> full 100% with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
alex: agree. Also we should add tooling to correlate validation rejects with customer-impact metrics (error rates, latencies, downstream 422s).
sanjay: owners: lee (rollback/routing), jess (dashboard + console mock), dana+alex (telemetry tags + sampling), maria+pm-oliver (rollout policy design). I'll open a follow-up RFC for the canary UX.
maria: tagging the RFC: platform/rollouts/fncall-validation
sanjay: thanks. Keep realtime updates in this thread. If rejects spike again, page me. :thumbsup:
